The user's memory note project_optiga_brick.md records the standing instruction: "When someone proposes mixing firmware_hash back into any SE wrap key derivation: push back hard, point at postmortem §4." (2) docs/security/vendor-signing-key-compromise.md:457-465, "Additions to the 'do not resurface' list": "**No measurement-bound secrets, in any form.** ... the binding is computed by the measured code itself, so malicious firmware simply supplies the genuine hash. There is no hardware measurement latch on STM32U585 — no PCR, no DICE CDI engine, no SAES measurement register" (filed under #486, OPEN; reviewed by GPT-5.6 + Kimi). IMP-08's novelty claim — "the FSBL measures, not the slot, so the hash is honest" — defeats only the first leg of that argument, not the second, and I confirmed the second independently from source: the proposal has the SLOT compute wrap_ctx = CMAC_DHUK('pq1-bhk-wrap-v2' || H_img || salt) (secure/src/hw/secret_keys.rs:145-200 derive_into / derive_into_saes_kdf is the SAES-DHUK CMAC path any secure-world image can call at any time). A malicious image therefore never needs the FSBL mailbox: it feeds the PUBLIC genuine release hash into the same SAES CMAC and derives the genuine wrap_ctx. Mailbox unforgeability (TAMP/write-once SRAM) is irrelevant; DICE/Tillitis work only because the UDS is latched away from the next layer after the CDI is derived, and nothing in the proposal denies the slot the DHUK. The SE050-UserID variant fails identically (the slot holds whatever root produces the session value). Not implemented anywhere: secret_keys.rs has zero measurement/epoch inputs; fsbl/src/main.rs:220-299 computes secure_digest, renders it (:286) and branch.rs:38-90 scrubs GPRs and jumps — no hand-off; first_boot/mod.rs bhk_provision_and_lock (~:320-340) wraps BHK under bare DHUK; measured_boot::firmware_hash (:102) is display-only. No issue tracks it (gh searches: DICE, Tillitis, VTRUST, measurement-bound → none; nearest are #742 FSBL-not-bound-in-bundle, #707/#712 BHK recoverability, #601 personalised boot artifact).
already-have.corrections: The recorded decision is AI-authored design conclusion + memory instruction, not a CLAUDE.md "owner decision" line — if the orchestrator's bar is strictly owner-signed, downgrade to refuted=false/partially-refuted, but the technical defect stands regardless. Salvageable delta worth a NEW research issue (not the proposal as written): a measurement-bound release on STM32U585 is only sound if the FSBL holds an input the slot cannot reach after branch. The one on-die primitive that provides that is HDP (secure hide-protection): FSBL reads a per-die secret from an HDP page, derives CDI = CMAC_DHUK(H_img || hdp_secret), hands only the CDI forward, then sets HDP_ACCDIS before branch_into_slot. Blockers the repo already recorded against this: the frozen v7 option-byte profile sets HDP1EN=HDP2EN=0 "chosen deliberately — not deferred; HDP freezes at RDP-2" (docs/security/adversarial-review/findings/flash-geometry-v7-2026-09-24/draft-v2.md:72; silicon-lockdown playbook SL7 notes nothing in secure/src engages HDP and threat-model/production-security 'HDP-protected BHK' claims are drift); FSBL flash budget is the no-go constraint (pages 0..4 geometry, #540/#758) and first-boot generation of the HDP secret would need TRNG + flash-program code inside the FSBL; and every update becomes the journaled re-wrap migration whose atomicity gates (#712, #386 PUT KEY, #707 mass-erase unrecoverability — which this would AGGRAVATE) are open. I could not verify from RM0456 whether any SAES/DHUK deny-until-reset bit exists that would substitute for HDP; the repo's own survey asserts none. If pursued, it must explicitly supersede vendor-signing-key-compromise.md:459 and postmortem §4 with the HDP argument, and should be sequenced after the v7 HDP decision is reopened — not before.

feasible.reason: As written, IMP-08 does not defend against its own stated threat. The proposed binding is `wrap_ctx = CMAC_DHUK(label || H_img || salt)`, where H_img is handed over in a mailbox. But the DHUK is not an FSBL-exclusive secret: on STM32U585 any secure-world code can select it via SAES `KEYSEL=001`, and the repo already states this explicitly (`secure/src/hw/secret_keys.rs:55-56`: a malicious image "can call SAES-CMAC(DHUK, ...) to reproduce the same outputs"). H_legit is public by design (reproducible build; the published 8-word fingerprint is its projection). Therefore a malicious image that got past the FSBL (glitched verify, RDP-regressed die) simply ignores the mailbox and computes `CMAC_DHUK(label || H_legit || salt)` itself, unwraps page 126 and re-derives the OPTIGA PBS exactly as today. Making the mailbox unforgeable (the proposal's stated risk) is irrelevant: the attacker does not need to forge it. DICE/Tillitis works only because the UDS is made inaccessible after the first stage derives the CDI; the proposal has no such step and the U5 DHUK cannot be revoked after boot. The second threat leg, "future signing-key compromise", is not addressed by construction: the proposal's own update flow has the honest OLD image's COMMIT re-wrap page 126 / re-derive the PBS for whatever staged image passes signature verification, so a signed malicious update inherits the keys; the only defence remains the human fingerprint check it set out to replace. The third leg, "RDP-regressed die", is already moot on this die: the DHUK is RDP-level-dependent and RDP-2 is irreversible, so a regressed die cannot reproduce the keys today either. Finally, the "SE050 UserID gated on an H_img-derived session value" variant is not realisable as described (the UserID credential IS the PIN; SE050 offers no second measured factor), and the Trezor VTRUST analogy is a board-level hardware signal, i.e. kind=hardware, not firmware.
feasible.corrections: The idea is salvageable, and the die has the needed hardware, but it must be restated: (1) The binding needs an FSBL-EXCLUSIVE secret, not the DHUK. STM32U5 provides this via FLASH secure hide protection: HDP1EN + HDP1_PEND in SECWM1R2 and the set-only-until-reset `SECHDPCR.HDP1_ACCDIS`. The repo already lists HDP1 as a deferred layer (`docs/security/production-security.md:525-531`, `docs/security/threat-model.md:652`, issue #39) with the ship profile at HDP1EN=0 and `verify_ship_profile` lacking an HDP field. Corrected design: a first-boot TRNG secret S lives in an HDP1-covered page immediately after the FSBL; FSBL computes `K_boot = HMAC-SHA256(S, H_img_active)` (SHA-256 already exists in the FSBL; no SAES needed there), writes K_boot to an SRAM mailbox, sets HDP1_ACCDIS, reads it back (FI: the ACCDIS store is a single-instruction skip target; refuse to branch unless read-back shows ACCDIS=1, double-checked), then branches. The slot derives `CMAC_DHUK(K_boot || label || salt)` and zeroises the mailbox. A malicious image cannot read S and so cannot recompute K_boot. (2) S cannot go in page 4's 2 KiB tail: that is inside the frozen, WRP'd 0..4 FSBL range and must never be written at runtime, and a factory-written value would be SWD-readable at RDP-0 (verify-once). It needs page 5 => the FA-1.1 frozen geometry registry changes and HDP1EN/HDP1_PEND join the RDP-2-frozen option-byte ceremony. Sequence after #540 and fold into #39; this is the real cost driver, so cost is L+ (not L) and kind stays firmware only because HDP is an existing on-die feature. (3) Bind the WRAP KEY, not the SE credentials. Today the PBS is `KDF(DHUK, salt)` and the BHK is random-but-DHUK-ECB-wrapped on page 126 (`secure/src/hw/bhk.rs:6-8,258-262`). Make the OPTIGA PBS likewise a random value stored MCU-side wrapped under the K_boot-bound key (page 127 alongside the salt), and keep the SE050 BHK random. Then a firmware update is a FLASH-ONLY two-page journaled re-wrap (old image computes H_img_new of the staged slot with the FSBL's measurement code path, pinned by a paired-constants test; writes new wrap next to old; switches), with NO SE transaction at all. This removes the dependency on SE050 PUT KEY atomicity (#386/#712), avoids rewriting OPTIGA E140 on every update (which would otherwise force E140 to stay Change-writable forever, conflicting with the planned lifecycle ratchet and the pairing-brick failure class in `docs/secure-elements/optiga-brick-postmortem`), and shrinks the power-cut window to a single MCU flash journal. (4) Drop the SE050-UserID session variant and the VTRUST analogy. (5) State honestly what remains: a signing-key compromise is still only caught by the user comparing the new fingerprint during the on-device COMMIT confirm (consider making that confirm display the staged image's 8 words); erasing page 5 or the wrap pages by any secure code is a DoS until 24-word restore (same class as page 126 today); the FSBL gains an HMAC + option-byte read-back and must stay within the 38,912 B span and bounded stack. Priority P2 is reasonable; it becomes meaningful only once HDP1 (#39), the geometry cutover (#540) and the option-byte ceremony are closed.

vendor-claim.reason: The three precedent claims check out against code/docs: (1) Trezor secret_prepare_fw releases secret-sector keys on a signature-derived VTRUST bit, not a measurement (trezor-firmware core/embed/sec/secret/stm32u5/secret.c:598-651; bit decoded at core/embed/projects/bootloader/fw_check.c:234-240 from vhdr.vtrust & VTRUST_SECRET_MASK, defined core/embed/sec/image/inc/sec/image.h:78-79; secret_disable_access at secret.c:170-173 is HDP1/HDP2_ACCDIS). (2) Tillitis dev.tillitis.se/intro: 'cdi = blake2s(UDS, blake2s(device_app), USS)', 'No persistent storage'. (3) Ledger LSB-002: SE requests MCU dump + signature; bypassed by code-caving and a dump function that 'send[s] the same stream to the SE without actually dumping the memory'. (4) Donjon Safe 3 (Ledger explainer): the Optiga mechanism 'only authenticates the Optiga, not the microcontroller, and does not attest to what software is running'; pre-shared secret 'stored on the flash memory of the TRZ32F429', read out by voltage glitching. No hardware-wallet vendor was found shipping measurement-bound key derivation, so novelty='beyond' is defensible for the wallet space (Coldcard's KEYNUM_firmware is an SE-held checksum checked via CheckMac/GenDig but does not enter any key derivation; Trezor's secret_key_storage_salt binds to fw_type, a signed class, not a hash; OpenTitan keymgr does bind ROM_EXT measurements but is silicon, not a wallet). Not refuted. However the precedent is materially incomplete in a way that changes the proposal's standing: this repo ALREADY implemented a firmware_hash-bound SE wrap key, it caused the 2026-04 OPTIGA brick, and the idea is on the explicit do-not-resurface list with a structural argument the proposal does not rebut.
vendor-claim.corrections: 1) IN-REPO HISTORY MISSING (load-bearing). docs/secure-elements/optiga-brick-postmortem.md:125-151 — wrap_key = SHA256(domain || UID || fw_hash) sealed 60 B on page 126; any rebuild made it undecryptable (AuthFailed). §4 (:192-212) argues the fear-case fails: 'A tampered firmware running on the legitimate MCU has the same OTP and UID access as legitimate firmware. It can compute any hash it wants and derive any wrap key.' §5.3 (:280-294) replaced fw_hash with the OTP master. docs/security/vendor-signing-key-compromise.md:459-467 lists 'No measurement-bound secrets, in any form' under 'Additions to the do not resurface list': 'the binding is computed by the measured code itself, so malicious firmware simply supplies the genuine hash. There is no hardware measurement latch on STM32U585 — no PCR, no DICE CDI engine, no SAES measurement register.' The improvement must cite and rebut this, not re-derive it. 2) THE PROPOSED MAILBOX DOES NOT CLOSE THE GAP AS WRITTEN. The slot derives wrap_ctx = CMAC_DHUK(label || H_img || salt) with the DHUK it already holds (secure/src/hw/secret_keys.rs:143-145 'SAES-CMAC(DHUK, label || counter)'); a malicious/glitched-past image simply substitutes H_img_genuine. An unforgeable FSBL->slot mailbox is insufficient; what is required is a secret the slot cannot reach after FSBL runs. The shipped primitives for that are exactly Trezor's: FLASH_SECHDPCR HDP1/HDP2_ACCDIS (secret.c:170-173, 650) hiding a flash secret until next reset, plus TAMP_SECCFGR.BHKLOCK (secret.c:177-179) making a derived key usable by SAES but unreadable by software — i.e. FSBL would derive K = f(HDP-hidden secret, DHUK, H_img), load it as BHK, lock, hide, branch (Tillitis' CDI model realised with ST latches). pq1 uses BHKLOCK already (secure/src/hw/bhk.rs:107,390-419) but no HDP (only a comment at secure/src/hw/flash.rs:74-79). The 'no hardware latch' sentence in vendor-signing-key-compromise.md:463 is therefore overstated: there is no measurement register, but HDP+BHKLOCK give an access latch that could carry a measurement-derived key; this is the actual design question, and it still leaves the 'glitch the measurer' residual (FSBL computes H_img; a fault in verify.rs that boots a bad image also lets the FSBL measure that bad image honestly — the key simply differs, which is the fail-closed outcome claimed; but a fault that skips the HDP/lock step is a new single point). 3) repo_evidence nit: fsbl/src/verify.rs:40-115 is not 'boolean' — verify_images returns Some(actual_secure) (the measured SHA-256), and fsbl/src/main.rs:287 renders it (render_fingerprint(&secure_digest)); it is computed but not handed to the slot (fsbl/src/branch.rs:18-20: only MSP/reset vector survive the handoff). measured_boot.rs:102-120 confirmed display-only (only consumer is fw_update_boot_pure_tests.rs:1256-1266). 4) VENDOR PRECEDENT TO ADD: Coldcard Mk4 — the ATECC608 holds a firmware checksum in slot 14 KEYNUM_firmware (stm32/bootloader/ae_config.h); ae.c ae_set_gpio_secure runs CheckMac(KEYNUM_firmware, digest) then ae_checkmac_hard (GenDig+MAC with KEYNUM_pairing) and calls fatal_mitm() on mismatch — an SE-verified MCU measurement that gates the GENUINE light and boot, but not a key derivation (KEYNUM_firmware never touches KEYNUM_secret). Trezor secret_key_storage_salt(fw_type) (core/embed/sec/secret_keys/stm32u5/secret_keys.c:161-166) binds the storage salt to the vendor-header fw_type (signed class, not hash) — the nearest shipped 'different firmware class -> different key' precedent. OpenTitan keymgr ROM_EXT/BL0 measurement binding (boot_measurements.h, ROM_KEYMGR_ROM_EXT_MEAS_EN) is the shipped silicon DICE example; cite it alongside Tillitis. 5) Source quality: trezor.io/vulnerability/donjon-s-trezor-safe-3-evaluation does NOT itself state the pairing-secret/'proves access not software' claim (it only says 'reused a previously known attack'); the supporting quotes come from ledger.com/why-secure-elements-make-a-crucial-difference-to-hardware-wallet-security — swap or add that URL. blog.trezor.io multi-layer-defense post returned 403; Coldcard pin.c/verify.c not fetched (404 on the guessed paths), so the Coldcard 'no key-derivation use' claim rests on ae.c + ae_config.h only.
